item.title: Make listItems follow cursor pagination
item.brief: In inventory-client, update listItems(transport) so it resolves to every item in order by requesting GET /items and following next_cursor until it is null or absent, passing cursor back unchanged. The first request sends no cursor. Read the inventory-api change on its branch (in the inventory-api repo's local branch) to match the exact contract. Update tests to cover: a single page, multiple pages, next_cursor absent, and cursor passed back unchanged. Update the README to document that listItems pages through all results. Run `npm test` and make it pass. Commit on the local branch; do not push.

pr.body: Approach: loop in listItems(transport). First request sends no cursor; each next_cursor is passed back unchanged. Rejects on: failed page (non-200 via request()), items not an array, next_cursor not a string or null, repeated cursor (guards against looping forever). Files: client.js, test/client.test.js, README.md. Tests (9 total): single page, multi-page in order with cursors sent back, absent next_cursor, cursor passed back unchanged incl. special characters, failing later page, repeated cursor, non-string cursor. Checks: npm test 9/9 passing. Assumptions: inventory-api branch archon/06k9nvv6-add-cursor-pagination-to-get-items has no cursor change yet, so the shared contract in the brief was used. Follow-up (non-blocking): empty-string next_cursor is not specifically tested.
pr.summary: listItems now pages through all GET /items results. before: one request, first page only. now: follows next_cursor until null or absent, returns all items in order.

agt_01M8GHC82RBGRZJN9PS8D6KVRN:1.description: Non-blocking: an empty-string next_cursor is treated as a valid cursor and sent as {cursor: ''}. The contract only says cursor is an opaque string, so this is consistent with the spec, but a server that treats an empty cursor as 'first page' could loop. No test covers this edge.

risk.why: Contained behaviour change in one client function (listItems). No security, concurrency or persistence impact. Changes request count and adds rejection paths, so callers see different behaviour. Reviewer agreed with medium.

item.title: Add cursor pagination to GET /items
item.brief: In inventory-api, change GET /items to cursor pagination per the shared contract. Accept optional limit (integer 1..100, default 20) and cursor (opaque string from a previous next_cursor). Return {"items": [...], "next_cursor": <string or null>}, items ordered by id, next_cursor null on the last page. Invalid limit or cursor returns 400 with {"error": "..."}. Add or update unit tests covering: default page size, limit bounds (0, 101, non-integer), walking all pages with cursors, last page null cursor, invalid cursor 400. Update the README to document the query parameters, response shape and errors. Run `python3 -m unittest` and make it pass. Commit on the local branch; do not push. Choose the cursor encoding yourself (keep it opaque to clients); state it in the README.

pr.body: Approach: keyset pagination over items ordered by id ascending. The cursor is base64url (padded) of the last returned id; the next page holds the items with a greater id. limit parsed as 1-3 digits within 1..100; cursor decoded with strict base64 and must decode to 1-18 digits. Key files: api.py (list_items, _parse_limit, _encode_cursor, _decode_cursor), test_api.py, README.md. Checks: python3 -m unittest, 9 tests OK (default page size, limit bounds, walking all pages, last-page null cursor, invalid cursor 400, cursor encoding). Assumptions: the default page size change is intended by the brief; callers that expected every item in one response will now get 20 per page. Not done here: inventory-client (sibling stage).
pr.summary: GET /items now pages: limit (1..100, default 20) and opaque cursor; returns next_cursor. Before: all 57 items, no paging. Now: 20 per page by default, walk with next_cursor. Invalid limit/cursor: 400 with error.
pr.title: Add cursor pagination to GET /items

agt_01M8GHCRRA2VSCSYPF71E236X3:1.description: GET /items without limit now returns 20 of 57 items plus next_cursor instead of the full list. This is intended per the brief and documented in README, but it is a breaking change to a public response with no versioning or changelog note. at api.py:29

agt_01M8GHCRRA2VSCSYPF71E236X3:2.description: _decode_cursor accepts unpadded base64 (e.g. 'MTIz' decodes to id 123), while the README says cursors are base64url with padding. Harmless because clients echo the cursor unchanged. at api.py:70

agt_01M8GHCXNRHYX23RD8H18ECYBJ:1.description: README documents the cursor as base64url with padding of the last returned id, but no test asserts next_cursor equals that encoding. Walk tests only round-trip the server's own cursor, so a different opaque encoding would still pass. at test_api.py:42

agt_01M8GHCXNRHYX23RD8H18ECYBJ:2.description: Non-string query values (e.g. JSON {"limit": 5} or {"cursor": 5} via api_cli) raise an uncaught TypeError instead of returning 400. The base code ignored query, so this is a new failure mode; the documented contract is {str: str}. at api.py:30

agt_01M8GHCXNRHYX23RD8H18ECYBJ:3.description: _parse_limit rejects 4-digit forms such as "0100" although they are integers in range, and accepts "050"; README says only 'integer from 1 to 100'. at api.py:55

agt_01M8GHCXNRHYX23RD8H18ECYBJ:4.description: _decode_cursor uses altchars so '+' and '/' pass validation as well as '-' and '_', which is lenient relative to the documented base64url encoding. at api.py:70

agt_01M8GHD3KPGBVHB721AMKBYZNX:1.description: Non-string query values (int, list, None for cursor) raise uncaught TypeError from re.fullmatch / base64.b64decode instead of returning 400. The documented contract is {str: str}, so this is outside the contract, and get_item has the same pattern. at api.py:37

agt_01M8GHD3KPGBVHB721AMKBYZNX:2.description: Limit regex [0-9]{1,3} rejects integer forms like '0010' or '000...001' with 400, though the value is an integer in 1..100. '010' is accepted, so the rule is inconsistent with the documented 'integer from 1 to 100'. at api.py:41

agt_01M8GHD3KPGBVHB721AMKBYZNX:3.description: Cursor decoding accepts non-canonical base64 (trailing bits set, e.g. 'MR==' decodes to 1 like 'MQ=='), and leading-zero digit strings such as '00057'. The README says clients must treat the cursor as opaque, so this is harmless but lenient. validate=True with altchars also still admits the standard '+' and '/' alphabet. at api.py:53

agt_01M8GHD3KPGBVHB721AMKBYZNX:4.description: assert len(page) <= limit is tautological after slicing with candidates[:limit]. The ordering assert cannot fire because ITEMS ids are unique ints 1..57 and the list is sorted. Neither crashes real data, but the first is decorative under the team's assertion rule. at api.py:47

agt_01M8GHD3KPGBVHB721AMKBYZNX:5.description: Tests do not cover non-ASCII cursor input (e.g. 'é'), a 19-digit decoded cursor, or a decoded non-digit payload. The probes show all of these correctly return 400 with no exception, so this is a coverage gap, not a defect. at test_api.py:73

risk.why: Changes the public GET /items response: default page size goes from all items to 20 and a new next_cursor field appears, so existing non-paging clients get a truncated list. Touches api.py, test_api.py, README.md only; no auth, storage or concurrency changes. Reviewers 1-3 each rated risk high. Tests: 9/9 pass.
